notes: All five tools are unconditionally registered in the single ListTools handler (build/index.js:101-378); there is no toolset gating, so every tool is default-enabled.
No filesystem, shell, or local network access anywhere in the file — only axios POST/GET to the five fixed api.tavily.com endpoints (build/index.js:20-26), hence no HOSTEXEC and no SECRET labels.
The Authorization header carries TAVILY_API_KEY (build/index.js:49) but the key is never echoed back into tool results, so it is not a SECRET exposure.

tavily_crawl.rationale: `crawl` sends the agent-chosen root `url` (plus free-text `instructions`) to Tavily's crawl endpoint; `formatCrawlResults` returns crawled page URLs and raw content, i.e. attacker-controlled web content (UNTRUSTED). The agent-chosen URL is requested by the crawler, so arbitrary data can be encoded into a URL on an attacker-controlled host (SINK). Crawling happens on Tavily's infrastructure, so no user-private data is reached.

tavily_extract.rationale: `extract` forwards the agent-supplied `urls` array to Tavily, which fetches those pages and returns their raw content via `formatResults` — arbitrary attacker-controlled page text enters the agent context (UNTRUSTED). Because the fetched URL is fully agent-chosen, the agent can embed data in the path/query of a host the attacker controls and that host observes the request, making this an exfiltration channel (SINK). The fetch is performed server-side by Tavily, so `file://`/user-localhost content is not reachable — not SECRET.

tavily_map.rationale: `map` passes the agent-chosen `url` and `instructions` to Tavily's map endpoint, which fetches the site and returns discovered links; `formatMapResults` puts those attacker-controllable URLs in context (UNTRUSTED), and the agent-chosen URL fetch on an attacker-owned host is an outbound channel the attacker can read (SINK).

tavily_research.rationale: `research` posts the agent-supplied free-text `input` to the fixed `https://api.tavily.com/research` endpoint and polls/streams back a synthesised report built from multiple web sources; `formatResearchResults` returns that web-derived text (UNTRUSTED). The remote research agent browses the open web driven by agent-controlled `input`, so it can plausibly be steered to request an attacker-chosen URL carrying exfiltrated data; the code gives no restriction on the research task, so the SINK label is kept (undetermined).

tavily_search.rationale: `search` POSTs the query to the fixed endpoint `https://api.tavily.com/search` (build/index.js:21,556) and `formatResults` returns titles, URLs, snippets and optional `raw_content` scraped from arbitrary web pages straight into the agent context — attacker-controlled content. The request goes only to a fixed vendor endpoint (no agent-chosen host), and `include_domains`/`exclude_domains` only filter results, so it is not a SINK; nothing local or credentialed is read, so not SECRET.

value_conditions.default: Key is read from env; keyless mode is used when absent
value_conditions.effect: Server runs in keyless mode; requests omit `api_key` and the API is expected to reject crawl/map/research with a recoverable envelope explaining a key is required, which is rendered as text (isKeylessEnvelope/formatKeylessEnvelope). The tools remain advertised in ListTools, so labels are unchanged for search/extract and only effectively degraded for the others by the remote API.
JSON object whose keys overwrite matching tavily_search parameters (e.g. can force include_raw_content or domain filters); does not remove any tool or label.
Prints tool descriptions to stdout and exits without starting the server (no tools callable).
